headings: Introduction
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Prepare the host machine before installing the Vast host software, including OS, BIOS, driver, power, thermal, and stability checks.
ranges: Prepare the host machine before installing the Vast host software, including OS, BIOS, driver, power, thermal, and stability checks.

headings: What should be ready before I run the host installer?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Before installing, make sure the host has supported same-type GPUs, native Ubuntu/Linux, an AVX-capable CPU, at least one physical CPU core per listed GPU, adequate RAM, fast SSD/NVMe storage, working compatible GPU drivers, stable public networking, and enough direct ports forwarded for both TCP and UDP.
ranges: Before installing, make sure the host has supported same-type GPUs, native Ubuntu/Linux, an AVX-capable CPU, at least one physical CPU core per listed GPU, adequate RAM, fast SSD/NVMe storage, working compatible GPU drivers, stable public networking, and enough direct ports forwarded for both TCP and UDP.

headings: What should be ready before I run the host installer?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: For Docker storage, the preferred setup is /var/lib/docker mounted on XFS with project quotas enabled in /etc/fstab; see Storage Setup.
ranges: For Docker storage, the preferred setup is /var/lib/docker mounted on XFS with project quotas enabled in /etc/fstab; see Storage Setup.

headings: What should be ready before I run the host installer?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: For verification, the self-test preflight enforces the current minimum thresholds (CUDA support, reliability gate, direct ports, PCIe bandwidth, internet bandwidth, VRAM, system RAM). The canonical list lives in Verification Stages: requirements.
ranges: For verification, the self-test preflight enforces the current minimum thresholds (CUDA support, reliability gate, direct ports, PCIe bandwidth, internet bandwidth, VRAM, system RAM). The canonical list lives in Verification Stages: requirements.

headings: What should be ready before I run the host installer?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: For CPU capacity, use the physical-core rule: the host should have at least one visible physical CPU core per visible GPU. Hyperthreads and logical CPUs do not count as physical cores.
ranges: For CPU capacity, use the physical-core rule: the host should have at least one visible physical CPU core per visible GPU. Hyperthreads and logical CPUs do not count as physical cores.

headings: How do I inventory a clean host?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Before changing drivers, disks, or networking, record the machine's starting state. This makes it easier to spot whether an install problem came from the provider image, the storage layout, the driver, or the Vast installer.
ranges: Before changing drivers, disks, or networking, record the machine’s starting state. This makes it easier to spot whether an install problem came from the provider image, the storage layout, the driver, or the Vast installer.

headings: How do I inventory a clean host?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages:
lsb_release -a
uname -a
lscpu | sed -n '1,25p'
lspci | grep -i nvidia
lsblk -f
findmnt /
findmnt /data0
findmnt /var/lib/docker
df -h /
ip -brief address
ranges:
lsb_release -a
uname -a
lscpu | sed -n '1,25p'
lspci | grep -i nvidia
lsblk -f
findmnt /
findmnt /data0
findmnt /var/lib/docker
df -h /
ip -brief address

headings: How do I inventory a clean host?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages:
Run the three findmnt checks separately. findmnt exits with status 1 and no output
when a target is not mounted; that can be expected for optional /data0, but it should
not hide the independent root and Docker-storage results.
ranges:

when a target is not mounted; that can be expected for optional /data0, but it should
not hide the independent root and Docker-storage results.

headings: How do I inventory a clean host?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Save the output somewhere private and redact public IPs or account details before sharing it. If /var/lib/docker is already mounted, Docker already has data, or old Vast services are still installed on a supposedly clean machine, resolve that before treating the host as freshly provisioned.
ranges: Save the output somewhere private and redact public IPs or account details before sharing it. If /var/lib/docker is already mounted, Docker already has data, or old Vast services are still installed on a supposedly clean machine, resolve that before treating the host as freshly provisioned.

headings: What Ubuntu versions should hosts use?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Use Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for new installs when possible. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS also works and may be useful when a driver or operational constraint requires it. Confirm the OS works with your GPU driver, Docker, storage setup, and the Vast host installer before listing a production host.
ranges: Use Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for new installs when possible. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS also works and may be useful when a driver or operational constraint requires it. Confirm the OS works with your GPU driver, Docker, storage setup, and the Vast host installer before listing a production host.

headings: What Ubuntu versions should hosts use?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Do not blindly copy old Ubuntu 22.04 cgroup-v1 workaround commands onto Ubuntu 24.04. Docker, kernel, and cgroup defaults differ by OS version; follow the current Vast host installer path for the OS you are actually using, and treat cgroup errors as install diagnostics to fix before listing.
ranges: Do not blindly copy old Ubuntu 22.04 cgroup-v1 workaround commands onto Ubuntu 24.04. Docker, kernel, and cgroup defaults differ by OS version; follow the current Vast host installer path for the OS you are actually using, and treat cgroup errors as install diagnostics to fix before listing.

headings: What NVIDIA driver version should I use?
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Use a stable NVIDIA driver that supports your GPU and a CUDA runtime compatible with the Vast self-test image family. Verification requires CUDA-compatible driver/runtime support for CUDA 11.8 or newer. Verify GPU visibility and driver health with nvidia-smi before listing.
ranges: Use a stable NVIDIA driver that supports your GPU and a CUDA runtime compatible with the Vast self-test image family. Verification requires CUDA-compatible driver/runtime support for CUDA 11.8 or newer. Verify GPU visibility and driver health with nvidia-smi before listing.

headings: BIOS, power, and stability
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Enable virtualization and IOMMU in BIOS if you plan to support VMs; check IOMMU guidance especially on AMD EPYC systems.
ranges: Enable virtualization and IOMMU in BIOS if you plan to support VMs; check IOMMU guidance especially on AMD EPYC systems.

headings: BIOS, power, and stability
claims.notice: Highlighted 1 passage for this statement on the page.
passages: Avoid riser, lane, power, or BIOS layouts that throttle PCIe bandwidth.
ranges: Avoid riser, lane, power, or BIOS layouts that throttle PCIe bandwidth.
